hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: LittleFS network root
inputs.revision: 10 MiB image written at NOR offset 0x600000; built-in flash verification passed. Kernel FIT #33 and SPL were preserved.

inputs.name: Preserved kernel FIT
inputs.revision: Kernel #33 FIT, 1,541,120 bytes; unchanged from the preceding SSH diagnostic acceptance.

inputs.name: Ports mDNS watcher-before-snapshot fix
inputs.revision: Ports main ec74c4d3c; shared mDNS patch f4b7c61df.

scenario: After writing only the new 10 MiB root to NOR on one reported V1.2 sample, perform an ordinary POWER boot with the installed kernel FIT #33 and SPL unchanged. Check WPA/IP, syslog startup and one logger nonce, then query the host mDNS A record, resolve its name with getaddrinfo, and make a strict pinned-key SSH echo by name. Do not restart mdnsd.
expected: The system boots from the installed NOR root; WPA/IPv4, local logging and automatic name resolution are available without restarting mdnsd.
observed: The ordinary POWER boot reached kernel #33 with the new LittleFS root mounted from flash1 and no panic was reported. WPA reached COMPLETED with SAE and PMF=1 and IPv4 was present. syslogd started through the configured service path and one unique logger nonce was read back. Without restarting mdnsd, a raw mDNS query received an A answer with TTL 10 and the correct address; getaddrinfo resolved the name, and strict pinned-key SSH echo by name exited 0.

measurements.name: name-based-ssh-echo-exit-status
measurements.unit: strict pinned-key SSH by resolved name

limits: One ordinary cold boot on one operator-reported V1.2 sample; repeated-boot reliability, long-duration stability and other board revisions are not established.

This observation confirms the scoped cold-start mDNS/name-resolution and local-logging path. It does not establish full Wi-Fi functionality, peer acknowledgement, Action-frame delivery, RRM or BTM acceptance.
The watcher-before-snapshot fix addresses the reproduced subscription-order race in the shared mDNS backend. This run does not prove it was the sole historical cause of the earlier startup failure.
Private logs, credentials, host keys, network identifiers and local paths are not published.
